public_rationale: This is a conditional bet: if someone carefully builds the full comprehension challenge, no current system will come close to humans. Searches found no such test as of the evaluation date. That means a well-funded, continuously refreshed, secure test with careful scoring, where systems watch full shows. Some long-video benchmarks exist, and one (LVBench) shows top models well below humans (67.4% vs 94.4%). But they lack the features he made part of the condition. Since the condition has not been shown to have happened, the forecast cannot be scored.
limitations: Whether a partial benchmark counts as 'carefully built out' is a judgment call.
Search may have missed a recent or obscure implementation.

statement.excerpt: But I am willing to wager that if someone put in that kind of effort and carefully built out the test, no current system would come close to human performance.
statement.document_title: AI has (sort of) passed the Turing Test; here’s why that hardly matters

from_speaker: if someone put in that kind of effort
would come close to human performance
our_interpretation: The condition is that someone builds the comprehension challenge he describes: a well-funded ($25-50M scale) test where systems watch full TV shows or films and answer questions. The questions are refreshed to avoid contamination, answers are scored carefully (perhaps by hand), and the machine is kept on the same footing as a first-time human viewer.
'Current system' means AI systems available around the post date, 2025-04-02.
'Not come close' means a large gap between the best such system and human viewers.
criteria.support_condition: A test meeting the condition is built, and systems from around April 2025 score far below human viewers on it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A test meeting the condition is built, and a system from around April 2025 scores at or near human level on it.
